blocks.text: All Group 2 metals burn in oxygen to form metal oxides, MO: 2M + O2 -> 2MO. Beryllium reacts with oxygen only at high temperatures (above 600 C) to form BeO, 2Be(s) + O2(g) -> 2BeO(s); a thin, strong oxide layer usually protects it and makes it less reactive than the other members. Magnesium burns brightly in air or oxygen to form magnesium oxide, and calcium reacts more vigorously still, with a brick-red flame.

blocks.alt: Four flame icons: magnesium brilliant white, calcium brick red, strontium crimson red and barium apple green.
blocks.caption: Flame colours of Group 2 elements (original diagram after Figure 17.2).
blocks.long_description: Group 2 metals and their compounds give characteristic colours when heated in a flame or burned: magnesium burns with a brilliant white light, calcium gives a brick-red flame, strontium a crimson-red flame and barium an apple-green flame. These colours make magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium compounds important in fireworks and flares.

blocks.text: The oxides of Group 2 are generally white solids and are basic; their basic character increases down the group. In water the oxide ion reacts to give hydroxide ions: O2-(s) + H2O(l) -> 2OH-(aq).

blocks.title: Basic oxide
blocks.text: A basic oxide reacts with water to form hydroxide ions (or with acids to form a salt and water). Group 2 oxides are basic oxides.

items: 2M + O2 -> 2MO; Be only above 600 C (protective oxide layer).
Group 2 oxides are white and basic; basicity increases down the group.
